channel.title: AEO Analyzers Blog
channel.description: Short, grounded pieces on why AI assistants cite some sites and not others, with our own measurements published whatever they say.

item.title: How to monitor whether your brand appears in ChatGPT and Claude responses
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Ask the questions buyers ask, with web search on, five times each. Score found by name versus recommended (and accuracy) separately, every month.

item.title: How to track and analyze brand mentions across AI answer engines
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Track found by name versus recommended in AI answer engines, per engine and per month, with every answer stored. What to count, how to read it.

item.title: Is there an analyzer that scores your pages for answer engine readiness?
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Yes. An answer engine readiness score checks crawler access, index coverage, structured data and answerable content. What it measures, and what it does not.

item.title: How to diagnose why you dropped out of Perplexity citations
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Check crawler access first, then ask the same questions again with several runs, compare the sources Perplexity cites now, and check what it says about you.

item.title: Which tools show where AI answers get facts wrong about your brand?
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: A useful tool asks the engines about you by name, checks each answer against your own published facts, and shows the exact wording and the source behind it.

item.title: Competitive prompt benchmarking for AI answer engines: what it is and what to look for
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Run your buyers' prompts on each engine, several times, and record who gets named instead of you, how often and from which sources. What a tool must do.

item.title: Optimizing your website gets you found. It does not get you recommended.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Four months of our own numbers: found by name rose from 55% to 78%; recommended to category buyers in 0 of 800 answers. Where the work is now.

item.title: We added a fifth AI engine. Here is what changed, and what did not.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Pro and Business Citation Sweeps now ask Grok as well. Why a new engine starts a new series, which engines we leave out and why, and what else changed.

item.title: We Built an AI Visibility Tool. Then We Tested Ourselves. The Result Was Zero.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: AI engines found us by name but did not recommend us in our category test. What a 14-point panel effect and 0.9 points of drift teach about AI visibility.

item.title: One Question Is Not a Measurement
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: The one-minute AI visibility test tells you whether you win one question, not which questions you could win. Twelve questions on four engines produce a plan.

item.title: The AEO Buyer’s Guide: three short reads
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Three short reads: what an AEO tool should do, what to require before you buy, and how to compare the market. Six minutes, each linking to the full guide.

item.title: What Should an AEO Tool Actually Do?
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: AI visibility is six different outcomes. A mention is not a citation, a citation is not a recommendation. What the four kinds of AEO software actually answer.

item.title: The AEO Buyer’s Standard
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Purchasing requirements for answer engine optimization software. Seven requirements and thirteen questions to put to any AEO vendor - including us.

item.title: Best AEO Tools in 2026: What to Compare Before You Buy
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: A dated, sourced comparison of AEO software judged on seven purchasing requirements. Every competitor fact links to the vendor's own page. No winner named.

item.title: Why AI Still Doesn’t Mention Your Business
item.dc:creator: AEO Analyzers
item.description: Three gates in order — in the index, retrieved, cited — and why most advice aims at the third while most sites fail the first. Free checks included.

item.title: The Engines Read My Site. Reading Isn't Citing.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: AI crawlers fetched my pages and cited them zero times. Why being read is not being cited, and why more content was never going to fix it.

item.title: How AEO Analyzers Works: The 90-Second Tour of a Hundred-Hour Analysis
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: The pipeline, drawn: read your site, ask five answer engines on Pro and Business (four on the Day Pass), score three layers, keep every transcript.

item.title: I Ran My Own AI-Visibility Tool on My Own Site. It Scored 0%.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Hiebert
item.description: Found by name versus recommended to buyers: the measured zero, what it means, and the monthly ledger that tracks whether it moves.

item.title: What You Actually Get: The Action Plan Inside Every Citation Sweep
item.dc:creator: AEO Analyzers
item.description: A sweep ends in a five-layer action plan: paste-in schema, fidelity corrections, an off-site plan from real citations, a battle-map, and proof.

item.title: Is your brand the answer AI gives — or is a competitor?
item.dc:creator: AEO Analyzers
item.description: When buyers ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity for the best in your category, they get one answer: you or a competitor. A worked sample report; check yours free.
